title: For a nuclear supply, software 1.9.9 was chosen instead of 1.10.0: an error in textual version sorting
description: Under agreed SemVer, 1.10.0 is newer than 1.9.9. We examine the established incorrect registry selection and verification of the minimum condition without unauthorized equipment updates.
seo_title: 1.9.9 or 1.10.0: an error in software version selection in supply
seo_description: Under agreed SemVer, 1.10.0 is newer than 1.9.9. We examine the established incorrect registry selection and verification of the minimum condition without unauthorized equipment updates.
seo_keywords: version comparison 1.10 1.9, nuclear supply software version, SemVer string sorting, minimum software version
content:
In a supply of nuclear equipment, software 1.9.9 was chosen as "the newest", although the manufacturer had already released 1.10.0. The reason turned out to be string sorting in the registry: the program compared characters, not numeric version components. If the Semantic Versioning scheme is agreed, the tenth minor version comes after the ninth regardless of the last patch digit.

How the registry chose an unsuitable release

In a conditional order for item I-4, a separate requirement is set: the provided software version must be no lower than 1.10.0 under the agreed Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 scheme. This is a specific condition of this supply, not a requirement of NP-071 for any item. The belonging of the releases to one software product and use of this scheme is confirmed by manufacturer documentation.

The available registry contains two normal releases: 1.9.9 and 1.10.0. There are no pre-release suffixes, additional build labels or special manufacturer rules in this comparison. Therefore the question can be resolved without guessing what unknown numbers on labels mean.

Automatic selection sorted the field as text and took the string that ended up last. After the identical characters "1.", "9" and "1" are compared. In the usual such order, the string 1.9.9 is placed after 1.10.0. It is precisely this that the system called the newest and transferred into the supply composition.

How these versions are compared under the adopted rule

A version is divided into major, minor and patch. First major is compared: here 1 and 1 are equal. Then minor: 9 is less than 10. At this point the order is already established: 1.9.9 is older than 1.10.0. The patch number 9 does not make the first release new, because by the rule the comparison does not reach patch.

The primary specification Semantic Versioning 2.0.0, clause 11, directly sets numeric comparison of the main components from left to right. Therefore the correct result of our selection is 1.10.0. The previously chosen 1.9.9 does not meet the minimum condition 1.10.0, although the registry supplied it with the "newest" mark.

The problem cannot be solved by turning the whole designation into a decimal fraction. The record 1.10.0 has three components, not a fractional part of one number. Also 1.9.9 is not the value 1.99. Removing the dots and comparing 199 with 1100 creates another rule that may give wrong results with a different number of digits.

Version number and completeness of acceptance are different checks

Correct order eliminates a specific selection error. It does not automatically prove that 1.10.0 suits all hardware executions or that it can be installed on operating equipment by oneself. For the supply, the provided checks of compatibility, composition and confirmation of result are preserved. In our example, a narrow question of meeting the established minimum number is now resolved.

There is no need to declare the previous 1.9.9 dangerous only because of its lower order. The reasons for a specific minimum requirement are determined by the related documents. Here it is enough that the established fact: the order requires no lower than 1.10.0, and the chosen release does not meet this condition.

If another manufacturer's numbering is not SemVer, it is considered by its rules. External similarity of "digits separated by dots" does not yet prove the required scheme. That is why in our case the contractual rule and product documentation are defined before comparison, not guessed from two strings.

How to fix automatic selection

The registry keeps the original full string and separately uses the provided version parsing mechanism. The control set includes both considered releases and the minimum condition. The corrected selection should obtain 1.10.0, and the check of 1.9.9 against the same minimum should give a negative result. This checks not only a neat list order, but also the final admission logic by number.

It is useful to additionally check the transition from 1.10.9 to 1.11.0: it shows that the fix did not reduce to manually rearranging two specific strings. For general rules with pre-release versions and build labels, full support of the adopted specification is needed. A simplified comparison of three numbers cannot be extended to all possible strings without considering their format.

If the erroneous selection has already been passed into the procurement specification, correcting the software list will not by itself change the task issued to the supplier. In the history they keep which release was originally chosen and for what reason it was replaced. Related lists should indicate one established composition, not different versions with the same "latest" mark.

The remark to I-4 can be closed specifically: "With string sorting, 1.9.9 was erroneously chosen. Under the agreed numeric SemVer order, release 1.10.0 is newer and meets the minimum condition; the previous choice did not meet it." If the supply disputes the version, send the question to NPI "Nedra" with the manufacturer's numbering rules and the order requirement, keeping full designations without abbreviations.
